certificate_policy: Each closed certificate was reconstructed from its script, had all dependency cuts eliminated, and passed the independent kernel.

theorems.name: zero_add
theorems.statement: forall n. 0 + n = n
theorems.summary: Zero is a left identity for addition; unlike PA3, this needs induction.

theorems.name: add_succ_left
theorems.statement: forall n m. S n + m = S (n + m)
theorems.summary: A successor can move through addition on the left.

theorems.name: add_comm
theorems.statement: forall n m. n + m = m + n
theorems.summary: Addition is commutative.

theorems.name: add_assoc
theorems.statement: forall n m k. (n + m) + k = n + (m + k)
theorems.summary: Addition is associative.

theorems.name: mul_zero_left
theorems.statement: forall n. 0 * n = 0
theorems.summary: Zero annihilates multiplication on the left.

theorems.name: mul_succ_left
theorems.statement: forall n m. S n * m = n * m + m
theorems.summary: A successor can move through multiplication on the left.

theorems.name: mul_comm
theorems.statement: forall n m. n * m = m * n
theorems.summary: Multiplication is commutative.

theorems.name: mul_add
theorems.statement: forall n m k. n * (m + k) = n * m + n * k
theorems.summary: Multiplication distributes over addition on the right.

theorems.name: mul_assoc
theorems.statement: forall n m k. (n * m) * k = n * (m * k)
theorems.summary: Multiplication is associative.

theorems.name: one_mul
theorems.statement: forall n. 1 * n = n
theorems.summary: One is a left identity for multiplication.

theorems.name: mul_one
theorems.statement: forall n. n * 1 = n
theorems.summary: One is a right identity for multiplication.

theorems.name: add_mul
theorems.statement: forall n m k. (n + m) * k = n * k + m * k
theorems.summary: Multiplication distributes over addition on the left.

theorems.name: succ_ne_zero
theorems.statement: forall n. ~(S n = 0)
theorems.summary: No successor is zero (the reusable PA1 lemma).

theorems.name: succ_injective
theorems.statement: forall n m. S n = S m -> n = m
theorems.summary: Successor is injective (the reusable PA2 lemma).

theorems.name: le_refl
theorems.statement: forall n. n <= n
theorems.summary: The defined order is reflexive; zero is its witness.

theorems.name: le_trans
theorems.statement: forall n m k. n <= m -> m <= k -> n <= k
theorems.summary: Order witnesses compose by addition, so the defined order is transitive.

theorems.name: no_succ_add_fixed
theorems.statement: forall p n. S p + n = n -> false
theorems.summary: Adding a positive successor cannot leave a natural number fixed.

theorems.name: drop_add_prefix_from_fixed
theorems.statement: forall a b n. (b + a) + n = n -> a + n = n
theorems.summary: A fixed-point equation remains fixed after dropping an additive prefix.

theorems.name: antisymm_from_witnesses
theorems.statement: forall a b n m. a + n = m -> b + m = n -> n = m
theorems.summary: Opposing additive witnesses force equality.

theorems.name: le_antisymm
theorems.statement: forall n m. n <= m -> m <= n -> n = m
theorems.summary: The witness-defined order is antisymmetric.

theorems.name: le_total
theorems.statement: forall n m. n <= m \/ m <= n
theorems.summary: Every pair of natural numbers is comparable in the defined order.

theorems.name: add_eq_zero_right
theorems.statement: forall a b. a + b = 0 -> b = 0
theorems.summary: A sum equal to zero has zero as its right addend.

theorems.name: mul_eq_zero
theorems.statement: forall n m. n * m = 0 -> n = 0 \/ m = 0
theorems.summary: Zero products have a zero factor: the 23-entry core capstone.

theorems.name: eq_symm
theorems.statement: forall a b. a = b -> b = a
theorems.summary: Equality is symmetric.

theorems.name: eq_trans
theorems.statement: forall a b c. a = b -> b = c -> a = c
theorems.summary: Equality is transitive.

theorems.name: succ_congr
theorems.statement: forall a b. a = b -> S a = S b
theorems.summary: Successor preserves equality.

theorems.name: add_congr
theorems.statement: forall a b c d. a = b -> c = d -> a + c = b + d
theorems.summary: Addition preserves equality in both arguments.

theorems.name: mul_congr
theorems.statement: forall a b c d. a = b -> c = d -> a * c = b * d
theorems.summary: Multiplication preserves equality in both arguments.

theorems.name: add_right_cancel
theorems.statement: forall a b c. a + c = b + c -> a = b
theorems.summary: A common right addend can be cancelled.

theorems.name: add_left_cancel
theorems.statement: forall a b c. a + b = a + c -> b = c
theorems.summary: A common left addend can be cancelled.

theorems.name: zero_le
theorems.statement: forall n. 0 <= n
theorems.summary: Zero is below every natural number.

theorems.name: le_succ_self
theorems.statement: forall n. n <= S n
theorems.summary: Every natural number is below its successor.

theorems.name: le_zero
theorems.statement: forall n. n <= 0 -> n = 0
theorems.summary: Only zero is less than or equal to zero.

theorems.name: add_eq_zero_left
theorems.statement: forall a b. a + b = 0 -> a = 0
theorems.summary: A sum equal to zero has zero as its left addend.

theorems.name: mul_ne_zero
theorems.summary: A product of two nonzero naturals is nonzero.

theorems.name: two_large_factors_impossible
script: have hzero : 0 = S a * S (S b) + b
have hzero' : S a * S (S b) + b = 0
have hprod : S a * S (S b) = 0
have hz : S a = 0 \/ S (S b) = 0
theorems.statement: forall a b. ~(2 = S (S a) * S (S b))
theorems.summary: Two naturals at least two cannot multiply to two.

theorems.name: prime_two
theorems.summary: Two is prime in the expanded first-order prime predicate.

theorems.name: multiple_zero
theorems.statement: forall a. exists q. 0 = a * q
theorems.summary: Zero is a multiple of every natural number.

theorems.name: one_multiple
theorems.statement: forall n. exists q. n = 1 * q
theorems.summary: Every natural number is a multiple of one.

theorems.name: multiple_refl
theorems.statement: forall a. exists q. a = a * q
theorems.summary: Every natural number is a multiple of itself.

theorems.name: multiple_add
theorems.statement: forall a n m. (exists q. n = a * q) -> (exists r. m = a * r) -> exists s. n + m = a * s
theorems.summary: Multiples of a fixed number are closed under addition.

theorems.name: multiple_mul_right
theorems.statement: forall a n m. (exists q. n = a * q) -> exists s. n * m = a * s
theorems.summary: A right multiple of a multiple remains a multiple.

theorems.name: multiple_mul_left
script: suffices hswap : m * n = n * m
theorems.statement: forall a n m. (exists q. n = a * q) -> exists s. m * n = a * s
theorems.summary: A left multiple of a multiple remains a multiple.

theorems.name: multiple_trans
theorems.statement: forall a b n. (exists q. n = a * q) -> (exists r. a = b * r) -> exists s. n = b * s
theorems.summary: The multiple relation is transitive.

theorems.name: not_multiple_pointwise
theorems.statement: forall a n. ~(exists q. n = a * q) -> forall q. ~(n = a * q)
theorems.summary: Turn a negated existential multiple into pointwise inequalities.

theorems.name: not_multiple_from_pointwise
theorems.statement: forall a n. (forall q. ~(n = a * q)) -> ~(exists q. n = a * q)
theorems.summary: Reconstruct a negated existential from pointwise inequalities.

theorems.name: add_residue
theorems.statement: forall a u c r s. r = a * c + s -> a * u + r = a * (u + c) + s
theorems.summary: Absorb a second quotient into an existing residue equation.

theorems.name: add_residue_lift
script: trans a * u + ((r + a * q) + t)
trans a * u + ((a * q + r) + t)
theorems.statement: forall a x u r q t c s. x = a * q + t -> r + t = a * c + s -> (a * u + r) + x = a * ((u + q) + c) + s
theorems.summary: Combine two quotient-and-residue summands and normalize the residue.

theorems.name: square_decomp
script: trans a * (q * z) + r * (a * q + r)
trans a * (q * z) + (r * (a * q) + r * r)
trans a * (q * z) + (a * (r * q) + r * r)
trans (a * (q * z) + a * (r * q)) + r * r
theorems.statement: forall a z q r. z = a * q + r -> z * z = a * (q * z + r * q) + r * r
theorems.summary: Expand a square while retaining an explicit quotient and remainder.

theorems.name: square_residue_lift
script: trans a * (q * z + r * q) + r * r
theorems.statement: forall a z q r c s. z = a * q + r -> r * r = a * c + s -> z * z = a * ((q * z + r * q) + c) + s
theorems.summary: Lift one quotient-and-remainder equation through squaring.

theorems.name: square_residue_witness
theorems.statement: forall a z q r c s. z = a * q + r -> r * r = a * c + s -> exists w. z * z = a * w + s
theorems.summary: Existential wrapper for the generic square-residue lift.

theorems.name: fourth_power_regroup
theorems.statement: forall n. n * n * n * n = (n * n) * (n * n)
theorems.summary: Regroup a fourth power as the square of a square.

theorems.name: mod5_residue_complete
theorems.statement: forall n. exists q. n = 5 * q \/ n = 5 * q + 1 \/ n = 5 * q + 2 \/ n = 5 * q + 3 \/ n = 5 * q + 4
theorems.summary: Every natural number has one of the five canonical residues modulo five.

theorems.name: mod5_nonzero_residue_cases
theorems.statement: forall n. ~(exists q. n = 5 * q) -> exists q. n = 5 * q + 1 \/ n = 5 * q + 2 \/ n = 5 * q + 3 \/ n = 5 * q + 4
theorems.summary: A nonmultiple of five lies in one of the four nonzero residue classes.

theorems.name: mod5_square_residue_one
theorems.statement: forall z q. z = 5 * q + 1 -> z * z = 5 * (q * z + q) + 1
theorems.summary: Squaring residue one modulo five preserves residue one.

theorems.name: mod5_square_residue_two
theorems.statement: forall z q. z = 5 * q + 2 -> z * z = 5 * ((q * z + q) + q) + 4
theorems.summary: Squaring residue two modulo five gives residue four.

theorems.name: mod5_square_residue_three
theorems.summary: Squaring residue three modulo five gives residue four.

theorems.name: mod5_square_residue_four
theorems.summary: Squaring residue four modulo five gives residue one.

theorems.name: mod5_fourth_power_residue_one
theorems.summary: A number congruent to one modulo five has fourth power congruent to one.

theorems.name: mod5_fourth_power_residue_two
theorems.summary: A number congruent to two modulo five has fourth power congruent to one.

theorems.name: mod5_fourth_power_residue_three
theorems.summary: A number congruent to three modulo five has fourth power congruent to one.

theorems.name: mod5_fourth_power_residue_four
theorems.summary: A number congruent to four modulo five has fourth power congruent to one.

theorems.name: mod5_fourth_power_one
script: have hsquare : n * n = 5 * ((x * n + 1 * x) + 0) + 1
have hsquare : n * n = 5 * ((x * n + 2 * x) + 0) + 4
have hsquare : n * n = 5 * ((x * n + 3 * x) + 1) + 4
have hsquare : n * n = 5 * ((x * n + 4 * x) + 3) + 1
theorems.statement: forall n. ~(exists x. n = 5 * x) -> exists x. n * n * n * n = 5 * x + 1
theorems.summary: A fourth power of a nonmultiple of five is one modulo five.
